history.dynasty: Chola origins; present masonry structure built by the Nayaks (16th century); endowments from the Cheras, Cholas and Pandyas
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the CSV gives town as Tiruppur, but the temple is at Avinashi, a panchayat town about 14 km from Tiruppur on the Chennai-Cochin highway (NH47). One of the most revered Shiva temples of Kongunadu, revered in the 7th-century Tevaram by the Nayanar Sundarar and classified as a Paadal Petra Sthalam; tradition calls it the first of the seven shivastalams of Kongunadu. Ancient name Tiruppukkozhiyur. Legend: two boys went to bathe in the temple tank and one was swallowed by a crocodile; on the mother's plea Sundarar sang praises of Shiva, and the boy emerged alive - the place Pukkoliyur ('where the boy came out of the crocodile's mouth') is named for this, and the relief of the crocodile with the child and Sundarar is carved at the base of the stone deepasthambham. The Tamil saying 'Kasiyil Vasi Avinashi' holds that worship here grants half the benefits of worship at Kasi (Varanasi); the Kasi well in the temple is believed to bring manifold benefits when bathed in on Amavasya, when the temple stays open all day. The five-acre complex has two gopurams (a 7-tier rajagopuram and a 5-tier gopuram for the separate east-facing Karunambigai shrine), with shrines for Sahasra Lingam, Pancha Lingas, Gaja Lakshmi, Chandikeswarar, Kala Bhairavar (in the inner prakaram - a rare feature), Navagrahas and Natarajar in a sabha mandapam. Administered by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department of Tamil Nadu.

name: Avinashi Lingeswarar Temple
town_description: Avinashi is an ancient panchayat town in Tiruppur district on the Chennai-Cochin highway (NH47), about 14 km from Tiruppur and 40 km from Coimbatore, historically part of Kongunadu and famed for this Paadal Petra Sthalam temple and the nearby Paadal Petra Sthalam Thirumuruganpoondi (5 km).

travel.airport: Coimbatore International Airport, about 40 km away, is the nearest airport.
travel.railway: Tiruppur railway station, about 14 km away, is the nearest railhead.
travel.road: On the Chennai-Cochin highway (NH47), Mangalam Road, Avinashi 641654; well-connected by buses from Tiruppur and Coimbatore.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; February-March for the Brahmotsavam and the Piranthanal Vizha.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-12:00 noon and 4:00-8:00 PM per most sources; Wikipedia notes six daily rituals from 6:00 AM to 8:30 PM, with no interval closing on new-moon days - verify locally.
